source.author: verg
source.text: Nec soli poenas dant sanguine Teucri; quondam etiam victis redit in praecordia virtus victoresque cadunt Danai: crudelis ubique luctus, ubique pavor, et plurima mortis imago.
source.text_original: Nec soli poenas dant sanguine Teucri; / quondam etiam victis redit in praecordia virtus / victoresque cadunt Danai: crudelis ubique / luctus, ubique pavor, et plurima mortis imago.
source.text_english: Nor do the Teucrians alone pay the penalty in blood; once even for the vanquished courage returns to their hearts, and the Danaans who had been victorious fall: cruel mourning everywhere, everywhere fear, and the grim presence of death in many forms.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: capti episcopi, interfecti presbyteri et diuersorum officia clericorum, subuersae ecclesiae, ad altaria Christi stabulati equi, martyrum effossae reliquiae: ubique luctus, ubique gemitus et plurima mortis imago.
reuse.text_original: capti episcopi, interfecti presbyteri et diuersorum officia clericorum, subuersae ecclesiae, ad altaria Christi stabulati equi, martyrum effossae reliquiae: ubique luctus, ubique gemitus et plurima mortis imago.
reuse.text_english: Bishops were taken captive, priests were killed, and the duties of the clergy of various ranks were overthrown; churches were demolished, horses were stabled at Christ’s altars, the relics of the martyrs were dug up: everywhere mourning, everywhere groaning, and a very great likeness of death.
